scope.description: Twelve Canadian company source leads for expanding verified Underwater ISR coverage, selected from durable first-party product and capability pages.

leads.sourceTitle: Underwater ROVs for Military & Police Operations
leads.leadSummary: Deep Trekker describes portable battery-operated ROVs with sonar and USBL options for underwater reconnaissance, threat assessment, diver overwatch, port security, and vessel inspection.
followUpQuestions: Which named ROV configuration is the best canonical capability record for defence use?
Which deployment, depth, endurance, and payload claims have product-level public documentation?

leads.leadSummary: Voyis describes high-resolution underwater imaging systems that combine subsea cameras, lighting, and compatibility with laser scanners for vehicle-based inspection and survey data collection.
followUpQuestions: Which Observer model should be the primary record and what depth and integration specifications are current?
Is there a durable public defence or security deployment source beyond general subsea inspection use?

leads.leadSummary: RBR presents Canadian-built oceanographic sensors that measure temperature, depth, salinity, dissolved gases, pH, and other parameters from deep ocean to polar environments.
followUpQuestions: Which single instrument or system has the clearest relevance to underwater operating-picture support?
Can a public defence, Arctic, or uncrewed-platform integration source corroborate mission relevance?

leads.leadSummary: International Submarine Engineering describes Explorer as a flexible long-range autonomous underwater vehicle and cites a continuous unsupervised under-ice survey exceeding ten days and one thousand kilometres.
followUpQuestions: Which Explorer configuration and payload options are publicly current?
What commercial availability, maturity, and recent programme evidence can be cited without relying on historic missions alone?

leads.leadSummary: Ocean Sonics describes icListen as a smart digital hydrophone for acoustic monitoring, streaming, recording, arrays, and onboard processing of underwater sound data.
followUpQuestions: Which icListen model and depth rating should anchor the capability record?
Which public defence or maritime-security deployment source supports a reviewed mission mapping?

leads.sourceTitle: SEAMOR Marine Ltd. - Durable Inspection Class ROVs
leads.leadSummary: SEAMOR Marine presents Canadian-built inspection-class underwater ROVs with integrated cameras, directional control, modular accessories, and configurations for observation and underwater work.
followUpQuestions: Which current ROV model is best suited to a first capability dossier?
What public defence, security, search, or infrastructure deployment evidence is available at product level?

leads.sourceTitle: Subsea Imaging Cameras, Lights, and Lasers
leads.leadSummary: SubC Imaging presents Canadian-engineered subsea cameras, lighting, lasers, DVR software, and remote imaging systems for inspections, surveys, and demanding underwater environments.
followUpQuestions: Which integrated system should anchor the record instead of treating the full catalogue as one capability?
Is there public evidence for defence, port-security, or critical-infrastructure missions?

leads.candidateCapabilityName: Naval sonar OEM systems and subsystems
leads.leadSummary: Nautel Sonar describes Canadian sonar products and subsystems, including hull-mounted and variable-depth wet-end systems and long-term support for Royal Canadian Navy underwater-warfare systems.
followUpQuestions: Which named sonar system or subsystem is appropriate for a public capability record?
Which RCN or allied programme claims have current first-party or government corroboration?

leads.candidateCapabilityName: Underwater acoustic defence systems and analytics
leads.leadSummary: JASCO describes underwater acoustic instrumentation, detection and localization software, Arctic hydrophone arrays, sonar-performance analysis, and components for Canadian naval anti-submarine-warfare upgrades.
followUpQuestions: Should the first dossier focus on OceanObserver, the Transient Detection System, or an integrated defence acoustics offering?
Which claims require separate Government of Canada or prime-contractor corroboration before publication?

leads.leadSummary: Xeos documents a fully submersible Argos beacon rated to eleven thousand metres for locating and recovering deep-ocean equipment after it returns to the surface.
followUpQuestions: Does recovery and location support warrant an Underwater ISR mapping or only a sustainment-support record?
What public integration examples exist for autonomous or defence underwater platforms?

leads.leadSummary: AML Oceanographic presents Canadian sensor, profiling, and moving-vessel systems for sound velocity, conductivity, temperature, depth, turbidity, and other water-column measurements.
followUpQuestions: Which profiler or moving-vessel product has the clearest defence or sonar-support relevance?
Can public deployment evidence support a mission mapping beyond general hydrographic sensing?

leads.candidateCapabilityName: Custom underwater acoustic sensors and systems
leads.leadSummary: Sensor Technology describes Canadian-built piezoelectric acoustic sensors and systems for high-value aquatic environments, including defence-prime and uncrewed-vehicle applications.
followUpQuestions: Which named sensor or system has sufficient public specifications for a capability dossier?
Can a first-party product page or public programme source support specific performance and deployment claims?
